title: Proper morphism with a finite fibre is finite near the base point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $S$ be locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $s\in S$ be a point such that the fibre $X_s=f^{-1}(s)$ is finite. Then there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that the restricted morphism $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is finite.

proof.text: Because a proper morphism is of finite type, the finite-fibre hypothesis at $s$ implies that $f$ is quasi-finite at every point of the fibre over $s$, by [pqf-lem-locqf-fibre-discrete] (using [pqf-lem-proper-basic] for finite type).

source.place: Tag 02OH proof, first sentence; Morphisms Tag 02NH

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq X$ be the open locus where $f$ is quasi-finite, supplied by [lem-sc-quasi-finite-points-open]. Since every point of $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ lies in this locus, $s$ is not in the image of the closed complement $Z=X\setminus U$.

The image $f(Z)$ is closed because $f$ is proper, hence universally closed by [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. Choose an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq S$ of $s$ disjoint from $f(Z)$. Then $f^{-1}(V)\subseteq U$, so the restricted morphism $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is locally quasi-finite by [lem-sc-quasi-finite-points-open].

source.place: Tag 02OH proof, definition of $Z$ through choice of $V$

proof.text: The restriction $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Since $V\to S$ is an open immersion, $X \times_S V = f^{-1}(V)$ and the projection is $f^{-1}(V)\to V$; by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] (1) it is proper. It is quasi-finite because it is locally quasi-finite and quasi-compact, using [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] and quasi-compactness from properness; hence it has finite fibres by [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres]. Applying [thm-pqf-finite-iff-proper-finite-fibres] to this proper morphism over the locally Noetherian scheme $V$ shows that it is finite.
